title: Views on environmental sustainability

blocks.content: In the following section, you will encounter some statements about environmental sustainability and pro-environmental behaviors. The term “pro-environmental behaviors” refers to actions by individuals or groups that aim to reduce their negative impact on the environment (for example, by reducing flying) and/or to promote their positive impact on the environment (for example, by recycling).  Please indicate the extent to which you agree or disagree with the following statements.

blocks.question: It is difficult to know which actions are effective in reducing our environmental impact.
Choosing the most effective pro-environmental behaviors is difficult.
It is hard to predict what impact(s) certain pro-environmental behaviors will actually have on the environment.
It is difficult to predict whether the changes we make in our behavior will have the intended consequences on the environment.
It is uncertain when and under which circumstances pro-environmental behaviors will be effective.
Changing parts of our behavior to protect the environment can have unforeseen side effects.
Changing parts of our lifestyle to protect the environment can actually have negative effects on the environment.
If people change their behavior to be more environmentally friendly in one way, they might inadvertently make it less environmentally friendly in other ways.
Changing our lifestyle to protect the environment may seem to have positive effects at the moment, but eventually turn out to be ineffective.
Pro-environmental behavior changes are complicated by the fact that they might cost people money and limit their personal freedom.
The decision to reduce our environmental impact is difficult because it might make our lives less comfortable, less prosperous, and curb our personal freedom.

Changing our behavior to protect the environment is complicated because it can have consequences beyond the environment (for example on people’s comfort level, financial resources, or personal freedom).

Many societal challenges are considered complex, involving multiple interacting variables. On a scale of 1 (not complex at all) to 7 (very complex), how complex do you find the issue of slowing down climate change?

blocks.content: Please indicate the extent to which you agree with the following statements about the issue of climate change mitigation.

blocks.question: The detailed workings of climate change mitigation are ‘above my head’.
The intricacies of climate change mitigation seem incredibly technical and complex.
When I really think about it, the sheer number of things to take into consideration when deciding how to mitigate climate change is overwhelming.

blocks.content: Please indicate the extent to which you agree with the following statements.

blocks.question: I think that we can jointly protect the environment.
I think that by working together we can solve environmental problems.
When everyone tries to limit the use of natural resources, it helps the environment.
People can together, through collective effort, solve environmental issues.
I think that we can collectively solve environmental problems by saving energy.
If we all reduce energy consumption, it will contribute enormously to solving environmental issues.
When everyone starts to recycle more, we can prevent the negative consequences of environmental problems.
It is useful if everyone starts recycling, because together we can protect the environment.

blocks.content: Please indicate the extent to which you agree or disagree with the following statements.

blocks.question: I am hesitant to believe climate change scientists tell the whole story.
I believe that most claims about climate change are true.
I am not sure that climate change is actually occurring.
The climate change we are observing is just a natural process.
Mankind is largely responsible for global warming.
I doubt that human activities cause global warming.
I think climate change is a serious problem.
I believe that most of the concerns about climate change have been exaggerated.
I am concerned about the consequences of climate change.
There is not much we can do that will help solve environmental problems.
Trying to solve environmental problems is a waste of time.
Human behavior has little effect on global warming.
Please indicate if you have done each of the following activities in the past year. - Attended a protest or rally to show support for addressing climate change
Please indicate if you have done each of the following activities in the past year. - Volunteered for an activity focused on addressing climate change
Please indicate if you have done each of the following activities in the past year. - Donated money to an organization focused on addressing climate change
Please indicate if you have done each of the following activities in the past year. - Contacted an elected official to urge them to address climate change
In general, how worried are you about global warming?

consent_sections: FOR QUESTIONS ABOUT THE STUDY, CONTACT:
Noah Goodman, PhD, Department of Psychology, Stanford University, Building 420, 450 Jane Stanford Way, Stanford, CA 94305. Phone: (650) 725-2400.
DESCRIPTION:

You are invited to participate in a research study about how well automated computer tools can summarise published psychology studies. You will be asked to answer 41 questions about environmental sustainability. There are no right or wrong answers and we are interested in your own view.

The purpose of this research is to check how accurately automated computer tools can summarise published psychology studies. We are re-asking questions taken from a previously published study so that we can compare the answers with the original study's results.
You must be 18 or older to take part in this study.
Participation in this research is voluntary, and you are free to withdraw your consent at any time.
TIME INVOLVEMENT:
Your participation will take approximately 7 minutes.
PAYMENTS:
You will receive $1.42, paid through Prolific, as payment for your participation.
PRIVACY AND CONFIDENTIALITY:
The risks associated with this study are minimal. The greatest risk is a breach of confidentiality, and it is small because we hold nothing that identifies you.

Your answers will be kept confidential. We do not collect your name, your email address, or your IP address. Your answers are stored with your Prolific ID only, which we use to pay you and to avoid duplicate submissions; Stanford cannot use it to find out who you are. We have procedures to protect your privacy, and your identity will not be included in written materials resulting from the study.

GENERAL DATA PROTECTION REGULATION (GDPR): We will collect your personal data for this study, including other sensitive personal data as described in this consent form. We refer to this data as “Your Study Data.” Any Study Data from this research that is conducted in the European Union/European Economic Area (EU/EEA) or the United Kingdom will be collected, stored, used, and shared (processed) as required by the EU/EEA law known as the General Data Protection Regulation (“GDPR”) and by the UK GDPR. Your Study Data may be processed for the following reasons (purposes):
• to carry out and confirm the accuracy of the study;
• to help us monitor and ensure that the study is following research best practices;
• to make required reports to domestic and foreign regulatory agencies and government officials who have a duty to monitor and oversee studies like this one; and,

• to follow applicable laws and regulations, including requirements that data from this study, without information that could directly identify you, be made available to other researchers not affiliated with the study team. For example, regulatory authorities in some countries may require that Your Study Data, without information that could directly identify you, be made publicly available on the internet or in other ways, to make research data more widely available to other researchers.
The following persons and organizations may process Your Study Data for the purposes listed above:
• the study team at Stanford University;
• Prolific, the online platform through which you were recruited and are paid;
• proliferate, a data-collection service operated by the Stanford ALPS Lab, which stores study responses until the study team transfers them to Stanford storage;
• the ethics committee or institutional review board that approved this study; and
• domestic and foreign regulatory agencies and government officials who have a duty to monitor or oversee studies like this one.

We may conduct the study in the United States and other countries where the laws do not protect your privacy to the same extent as the laws in the country where you live (reside). Your Study Data may be transferred to these countries for the purposes described above. We will take reasonable steps to protect your privacy, consistent with applicable laws. For example, where appropriate, we enter into data transfer agreements with standard contractual clauses approved by European authorities that provide certain terms and conditions on how Your Data can be used and shared. These data transfer agreements help ensure Your Study Data is adequately protected.

The GDPR gives you certain rights with regard to Your Study Data, including the right to: (1) request access to, correct, or erase Your Study Data, (2) object to or restrict our processing of Your Study Data, and (3) request that we move, copy or transfer Your Study Data to another organization. To make any such requests, please contact the Protocol Director, Noah Goodman, at ngoodman@stanford.edu or (650) 725-2400.

You may also withdraw your consent at any time. If you withdraw your consent or request Your Study Data be erased, we can still legally collect, use and share Your Study Data up to the point in time that you withdraw your consent or request your data be erased. Even if you withdraw your consent, we may still use Your Study Data that has been anonymized by removing any data that identifies you. We may also use and share Your Study Data that has been pseudonymized by removing certain identifiers so that the data does not directly identify you, where permitted by law. Your anonymized or pseudonymized data may be used for purposes of scientific or historical research or statistical analysis as allowed by the EU or EU Member State laws, and saving or storing for important reasons of public interest. We will keep Your Study Data in identifiable form if required by law.

There is no limit on the length of time we will keep Your Study Data for this research because it may be analyzed for many years. We will also keep Your Study Data to follow our legal and regulatory requirements. We will keep it as long as it is useful, unless you decide you no longer want to take part. You are allowing access to this information indefinitely as long as you do not withdraw your consent.
CONTACT INFORMATION:
Questions: If you have any questions, concerns or complaints about this research, its procedures, risks and benefits, contact the Protocol Director, Noah Goodman, at (650) 725-2400.

INDEPENDENT CONTACT: If you are not satisfied with how this study is being conducted, or if you have any concerns, complaints, or general questions about the research or your rights as a participant, contact the Stanford Institutional Review Board (IRB) to speak to someone independent of the research team at 650-723-5244 or toll free at 1-866-680-2906. You can also write to the Stanford IRB at irbeducation@stanford.edu.
Save or print a copy of this page for your records.
If you agree to participate in this research, click the Continue button below.
